symbols.name: Command
symbols.doc: Command is one Exec*= command, its prefixes parsed.

symbols.name: CommandFlags
symbols.doc: CommandFlags are the prefixes of one Exec*= command.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config is one service unit: systemd.service(5)'s directives as typed
values, the template its commands are spawned from, and the ports — the
engine's configuration (ADR 0214 §9).

symbols.name: Event
symbols.doc: Event is one published change of a unit.

symbols.name: ExitStatusSet
symbols.doc:
ExitStatusSet is SuccessExitStatus=, RestartPreventExitStatus= or
RestartForceExitStatus=.

symbols.name: ExitType
symbols.doc: ExitType is ExitType=.

symbols.name: ExitTypeCgroup
symbols.doc:
ExitTypeCgroup ends the unit when its cgroup is empty; it needs a
CgroupUnit.

symbols.name: ExitTypeMain
symbols.doc: ExitTypeMain ends the unit when its main process exits.

symbols.name: FlagArgv0
symbols.doc:
FlagArgv0 is "@": the second word is argv[0]; with FlagShell, the shell is
a login shell.

symbols.name: FlagFullPrivileges
symbols.doc:
FlagFullPrivileges is "+": the command runs without the unit's credentials
and confinement, on Config.AllowPrivilegedControl only.

symbols.name: FlagIgnoreFailure
symbols.doc: FlagIgnoreFailure is "-": a failure is recorded and read as a success.

symbols.name: FlagNoCredentials
symbols.doc:
FlagNoCredentials is "!": the command runs without User=, Group= and
SupplementaryGroups=, on Config.AllowPrivilegedControl only.

symbols.name: FlagNoEnvExpand
symbols.doc: FlagNoEnvExpand is ":": $VAR and ${VAR} are not expanded.

symbols.name: FlagShell
symbols.doc:
FlagShell is "|": the command runs through the shell's -c, or is the shell
alone.

symbols.name: Freeze
symbols.doc:
Freeze hands units over (S0h): each unit's actor ends without stopping
a process, its state and descriptors kept in the hand-over.

symbols.name: Handover
symbols.doc:
Handover is what an outgoing image hands the incoming one (S0h): Freeze,
Reexec, TakeHandover, Resume.

symbols.name: Infinity
symbols.doc:
Infinity is systemd's "infinity" for a duration directive: no timeout, a
start-limit window that never ends, no ceiling on the restart delay.

symbols.name: KillMode
symbols.doc: KillMode is KillMode=; its zero is control-group with a CgroupUnit.

symbols.name: KillModeControlGroup
symbols.doc:
KillModeControlGroup signals every process of the unit's cgroup and
waits for it to be empty; it needs a CgroupUnit.

symbols.name: KillModeDefault
symbols.doc:
KillModeDefault is control-group for a unit whose Cgroup is a
CgroupUnit, process for any other.

symbols.name: KillModeMixed
symbols.doc:
KillModeMixed signals the main and control processes, then kills the
whole cgroup; it needs a CgroupUnit.

symbols.name: KillModeNone
symbols.doc:
KillModeNone signals nothing: the stop commands run, the processes are
left.

symbols.name: KillModeProcess
symbols.doc: KillModeProcess signals the main and control processes only.

symbols.name: ListenNotify
symbols.doc:
ListenNotify opens an sd_notify socket for one unit; off Linux and
FreeBSD it is UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.

symbols.name: NewAttacher
symbols.doc:
NewAttacher is the Attacher over proc/process's Attach and AttachPIDFile, a
PID file nobody vouches for bounded by scope; on Linux, darwin and the
BSDs.

symbols.name: NewUnit
symbols.doc: NewUnit checks cfg and starts an inactive unit; Start starts it.

symbols.name: Notification
symbols.doc: Notification is one sd_notify message as a NotifySource hands it over.

symbols.name: NotifyAccess
symbols.doc: NotifyAccess is NotifyAccess=.

symbols.name: NotifyAccessAll
symbols.doc:
NotifyAccessAll reads the messages of every process of the unit's cgroup;
it needs the unit's cgroup.

symbols.name: NotifyAccessExec
symbols.doc:
NotifyAccessExec reads the main and the control processes' messages; it
needs the unit's cgroup.

symbols.name: NotifyAccessMain
symbols.doc: NotifyAccessMain reads the main process's messages.

symbols.name: NotifyAccessNone
symbols.doc: NotifyAccessNone reads no message.

symbols.name: NotifySource
symbols.doc: NotifySource is where a unit's sd_notify messages come from.

symbols.name: OOMPolicy
symbols.doc: OOMPolicy is OOMPolicy=.

symbols.name: OOMPolicyContinue
symbols.doc: OOMPolicyContinue keeps the unit running after an OOM kill.

symbols.name: OOMPolicyDefault
symbols.doc: OOMPolicyDefault is stop, or continue under Delegate=.

symbols.name: OOMPolicyKill
symbols.doc:
OOMPolicyKill has the kernel kill the whole cgroup (memory.oom.group),
the unit ending with the result oom-kill.

symbols.name: OOMPolicyStop
symbols.doc: OOMPolicyStop stops the unit, which ends with the result oom-kill.

symbols.name: OpenImage
symbols.doc: OpenImage opens the program a re-exec runs, O_PATH and close-on-exec.

symbols.name: ParseCommand
symbols.doc:
ParseCommand reads one Exec*= command from its words, its prefixes
"@-:+!|" parsed.

symbols.name: Preserve
symbols.doc: Preserve is FileDescriptorStorePreserve=.

symbols.name: PreserveNo
symbols.doc: PreserveNo releases the store when the unit stops.

symbols.name: PreserveOnSuccess
symbols.doc:
PreserveOnSuccess is PreserveYes, released once the unit is failed for
good.

symbols.name: PreserveRestart
symbols.doc:
PreserveRestart keeps the store while the unit is neither inactive nor
failed, or is about to restart.

symbols.name: PreserveYes
symbols.doc: PreserveYes keeps the store until the unit is removed.

symbols.name: PrivateTmp
symbols.doc: PrivateTmp is PrivateTmp=.

symbols.name: PrivateTmpDisconnected
symbols.doc:
PrivateTmpDisconnected mounts a new tmpfs, mode 1777, on /tmp and on
/var/tmp for each command.

symbols.name: PrivateTmpNo
symbols.doc: PrivateTmpNo shares the host's /tmp and /var/tmp — the zero.

symbols.name: PrivateTmpYes
symbols.doc:
PrivateTmpYes, directories on the host shared by every command of the unit,
is refused (DIRECTIVE_UNSUPPORTED).

symbols.name: ProtectSystem
symbols.doc: ProtectSystem is ProtectSystem=.

symbols.name: ProtectSystemFull
symbols.doc: ProtectSystemFull makes /etc read-only too.

symbols.name: ProtectSystemNo
symbols.doc: ProtectSystemNo leaves every tree writable — the zero.

symbols.name: ProtectSystemStrict
symbols.doc:
ProtectSystemStrict, the whole hierarchy read-only but /dev, /proc and /sys,
is refused (DIRECTIVE_UNSUPPORTED).

symbols.name: ProtectSystemYes
symbols.doc: ProtectSystemYes makes /usr read-only, and /boot and /efi where they exist.

symbols.name: Reexec
symbols.doc:
Reexec executes image again in this process, handing it h; it returns
only when the kernel refused (REEXEC_FAILED).

symbols.name: Restart
symbols.doc: Restart is Restart=.

symbols.name: RestartAlways
symbols.doc: RestartAlways restarts after every end but a skipped condition.

symbols.name: RestartMode
symbols.doc: RestartMode is RestartMode=.

symbols.name: RestartModeDebug
symbols.doc:
RestartModeDebug is RestartModeNormal, and the restarted unit's processes
get DEBUG_INVOCATION=1.

symbols.name: RestartModeDirect
symbols.doc: RestartModeDirect goes to auto-restart without publishing the failure.

symbols.name: RestartModeNormal
symbols.doc:
RestartModeNormal publishes the failed (or inactive) state, then auto-
restart.

symbols.name: RestartNo
symbols.doc: RestartNo never restarts.

symbols.name: RestartOnAbnormal
symbols.doc:
RestartOnAbnormal restarts after an unclean signal, a timeout, a watchdog,
an OOM kill — not after an exit code.

symbols.name: RestartOnAbort
symbols.doc: RestartOnAbort restarts after an unclean signal only.

symbols.name: RestartOnFailure
symbols.doc:
RestartOnFailure restarts after an unclean exit code, an unclean signal, a
timeout, a watchdog, an OOM kill.

symbols.name: RestartOnSuccess
symbols.doc: RestartOnSuccess restarts after a clean end only.

symbols.name: RestartOnWatchdog
symbols.doc: RestartOnWatchdog restarts after a watchdog only.

symbols.name: Result
symbols.doc: Result is why a run of a unit ended: systemd's Result=.

symbols.name: ResultCoreDump
symbols.doc: ResultCoreDump is an unclean signal that dumped core.

symbols.name: ResultExecCondition
symbols.doc: ResultExecCondition is an ExecCondition= that said skip.

symbols.name: ResultExitCode
symbols.doc: ResultExitCode is an unclean exit code.

symbols.name: ResultOOMKill
symbols.doc: ResultOOMKill is an OOM kill in the unit's cgroup (S0g).

symbols.name: ResultProtocol
symbols.doc: ResultProtocol is a notify unit whose main process ended before READY=1.

symbols.name: ResultResources
symbols.doc: ResultResources is a command that could not be spawned.

symbols.name: ResultSignal
symbols.doc: ResultSignal is an unclean signal.

symbols.name: ResultStartLimitHit
symbols.doc: ResultStartLimitHit is a start the limiter refused.

symbols.name: ResultSuccess
symbols.doc: ResultSuccess is a clean end.

symbols.name: ResultTimeout
symbols.doc: ResultTimeout is a start, stop, reload or runtime limit that expired.

symbols.name: ResultWatchdog
symbols.doc: ResultWatchdog is a missed keep-alive, WATCHDOG=trigger, or Fail.

symbols.name: Resume
symbols.doc:
Resume makes the unit cfg names from the state h holds for it: its
processes held again, its timers, watches and store as they were.

symbols.name: Snapshot
symbols.doc: Snapshot is a unit at one instant: what Unit.State returns.

symbols.name: SpawnInstance
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, template *Config, instance string, conn *os.File) (*Unit, error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, template *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/service.Config, instance string, conn *os.File) (*github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/service.Unit, error)
symbols.doc:
SpawnInstance makes and starts the unit of one accepted connection
(Accept=yes): a copy of template named instance, conn handed to its
ExecStart= at fd 3 and closed at its end; the unit is returned with
Start's error once it was made.

symbols.name: Spawner
symbols.doc: Spawner starts the processes of a unit; proc/exec's Start by default.

symbols.name: State
symbols.doc: State is where a unit stands.

symbols.name: StateActivating
symbols.doc:
StateActivating is starting: a condition, the pre-start commands, the main
process before it is up, the post-start commands.

symbols.name: StateActive
symbols.doc: StateActive is up.

symbols.name: StateAutoRestart
symbols.doc: StateAutoRestart is waiting out the restart delay.

symbols.name: StateConditionSkipped
symbols.doc: StateConditionSkipped is not running because ExecCondition= said so.

symbols.name: StateDeactivating
symbols.doc:
StateDeactivating is stopping: the stop commands, the signals, the post-
stop commands.

symbols.name: StateExited
symbols.doc: StateExited is up with no process left: RemainAfterExit=.

symbols.name: StateFailed
symbols.doc: StateFailed is not running, after a failure.

symbols.name: StateInactive
symbols.doc: StateInactive is not running, after a success or before any start.

symbols.name: StateReloading
symbols.doc: StateReloading is reloading.

symbols.name: StoredFD
symbols.doc: StoredFD is one descriptor of a unit's store, as Unit.FDStore lists it.

symbols.name: Sub
symbols.doc: Sub is the step a unit is at: systemd's SubState.

symbols.name: SubAutoRestart
symbols.doc: SubAutoRestart waits out the restart delay.

symbols.name: SubCondition
symbols.doc: SubCondition runs ExecCondition=.

symbols.name: SubDead
symbols.doc: SubDead is inactive.

symbols.name: SubExited
symbols.doc: SubExited is up without a process (RemainAfterExit=).

symbols.name: SubFailed
symbols.doc: SubFailed is failed.

symbols.name: SubFinalSigkill
symbols.doc:
SubFinalSigkill waits after FinalKillSignal= sent to what ExecStopPost=
left.

symbols.name: SubFinalSigterm
symbols.doc: SubFinalSigterm waits after KillSignal= sent to what ExecStopPost= left.

symbols.name: SubFinalWatchdog
symbols.doc:
SubFinalWatchdog waits after WatchdogSignal= sent to what ExecStopPost=
left.

symbols.name: SubReload
symbols.doc: SubReload runs ExecReload=.

symbols.name: SubReloadNotify
symbols.doc: SubReloadNotify waits for READY=1 after RELOADING=1.

symbols.name: SubReloadPost
symbols.doc: SubReloadPost runs ExecReloadPost=.

symbols.name: SubReloadSignal
symbols.doc: SubReloadSignal waits for RELOADING=1 after ReloadSignal=.

symbols.name: SubRunning
symbols.doc: SubRunning is up with its main process.

symbols.name: SubRunningRevalidating
symbols.doc:
SubRunningRevalidating is a Type=dbus unit up without its BusName= owned,
given two seconds to own it again before it stops.

symbols.name: SubStart
symbols.doc: SubStart runs ExecStart= until the unit is up.

symbols.name: SubStartPost
symbols.doc: SubStartPost runs ExecStartPost=.

symbols.name: SubStartPre
symbols.doc: SubStartPre runs ExecStartPre=.

symbols.name: SubStop
symbols.doc: SubStop runs ExecStop=.

symbols.name: SubStopPost
symbols.doc: SubStopPost runs ExecStopPost=.

symbols.name: SubStopSigkill
symbols.doc: SubStopSigkill waits after FinalKillSignal=.

symbols.name: SubStopSigterm
symbols.doc: SubStopSigterm waits after KillSignal=.

symbols.name: SubStopWatchdog
symbols.doc: SubStopWatchdog waits after WatchdogSignal=.

symbols.name: SystemCallFilter
symbols.doc: SystemCallFilter is SystemCallFilter=, an allow-list or a deny-list.

symbols.name: TakeHandover
symbols.doc:
TakeHandover reads the hand-over the outgoing image left this one; a
refused one leaves no descriptor open and no child unsupervised.

symbols.name: TemporaryFileSystem
symbols.doc: TemporaryFileSystem is one entry of TemporaryFileSystem=.

symbols.name: TimeoutAbort
symbols.doc:
TimeoutAbort sends WatchdogSignal=, then FinalKillSignal= after
TimeoutAbortSec=.

symbols.name: TimeoutKill
symbols.doc: TimeoutKill sends FinalKillSignal= at once.

symbols.name: TimeoutMode
symbols.doc: TimeoutMode is TimeoutStartFailureMode= or TimeoutStopFailureMode=.

symbols.name: TimeoutTerminate
symbols.doc:
TimeoutTerminate sends KillSignal=, then FinalKillSignal= after
TimeoutStopSec=.

symbols.name: Toggle
symbols.doc: Toggle is a boolean directive whose default is yes.

symbols.name: ToggleDefault
symbols.doc: ToggleDefault is the directive's default.

symbols.name: ToggleNo
symbols.doc: ToggleNo is no.

symbols.name: ToggleYes
symbols.doc: ToggleYes is yes.

symbols.name: Type
symbols.doc: Type is Type=.

symbols.name: TypeDbus
symbols.doc:
TypeDbus is up once its main process runs and its BusName= is owned on the
bus, and stops when the name is lost (Linux; a BusWatcher follows it).

symbols.name: TypeDefault
symbols.doc:
TypeDefault resolves to TypeDbus with a BusName=, else to TypeSimple with
an ExecStart=, to TypeOneshot without.

symbols.name: TypeExec
symbols.doc: TypeExec is up once its main process has executed its binary.

symbols.name: TypeForking
symbols.doc:
TypeForking is up once the process it spawned exits, the daemon it forked
adopted from PIDFile= (S0c; refused until then).

symbols.name: TypeIdle
symbols.doc:
TypeIdle runs as TypeSimple: the job queue systemd delays it behind is the
caller's.

symbols.name: TypeNotify
symbols.doc: TypeNotify is up once its main process sends READY=1.

symbols.name: TypeNotifyReload
symbols.doc:
TypeNotifyReload is TypeNotify whose reload is ReloadSignal= followed by
RELOADING=1 and READY=1.

symbols.name: TypeOneshot
symbols.doc:
TypeOneshot is up once its main processes ran to a successful end, one
ExecStart= after the other.

symbols.name: TypeSimple
symbols.doc: TypeSimple is up once its main process is spawned.

symbols.name: Unit
symbols.doc:
Unit is one service unit, driven by one actor over a pure reducer (ADR
0214 §3).

symbols.name: Zero
symbols.doc:
Zero is systemd's literal 0 for a duration directive, where it differs
from the default the Go zero value asks for: RestartSec=0 restarts at
once, StartLimitIntervalSec=0 disables the limiter, and a timeout of 0 is
no timeout.

symbols.name: Cause
symbols.doc:
Cause is the cause a NotifyContext context is cancelled with: the signal
that arrived. It aliases the service value.

symbols.name: CauseSignal
symbols.doc: CauseSignal reports the signal a NotifyContext context was cancelled by.

symbols.name: Escalate
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, clk clock.Waiter, policy Escalation, sigs ...Signal) (stop func())
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, clk github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/clock.Waiter, policy github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/signal.Escalation, sigs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/signal.Signal) (stop func())
symbols.doc:
Escalate runs policy.OnFirst at a delivery of one of sigs and policy.OnRepeat
once at a second delivery within policy.Window on clk — zero meaning any
later one — then stops relaying: the "second Ctrl-C stops at once"
convention. stop is idempotent.

symbols.name: Escalation
symbols.doc:
Escalation is the policy Escalate applies: OnFirst, OnRepeat and the
Window between them. It aliases the service value.

symbols.name: Notify
symbols.doc:
Notify subscribes to sigs and returns a receive-only channel of typed Signals
plus an idempotent, leak-free stop function. Each delivery is translated to a
typed Signal; the channel is buffered so a burst is not dropped, and stop
detaches the subscription and closes the channel.

symbols.name: NotifyContext
symbols.spelled: func(parent context.Context, sigs ...Signal) (ctx context.Context, stop func())
symbols.canonical: func(parent context.Context, sigs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/signal.Signal) (ctx context.Context, stop func())
symbols.doc:
NotifyContext returns a copy of parent cancelled when one of sigs arrives,
with a Cause naming it — os/signal's NotifyContext for the typed Signal.
stop unsubscribes and ends the bridge; it is idempotent.

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.doc:
Parse resolves a signal from its name or number — the canonical "SIGTERM", the
bare "TERM", or the numeric "15", all case-insensitive, and on Linux and
FreeBSD the realtime "SIGRTMIN+n" / "SIGRTMAX-n" — returning a typed
UNKNOWN_SIGNAL error for anything the platform does not define.

symbols.name: Relay
symbols.doc:
Relay reads signals from src and forwards each to target until src closes —
via kill(2) on Unix, via TerminateProcess or a console control event on
Windows. A positive target is a pid; a target below -1 addresses the process
group whose id is -target. It returns nil on a clean drain and a typed
RELAY_FAILED error on the first delivery failure (UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM on a
platform that is neither Unix nor Windows).

symbols.name: SendValue
symbols.spelled: func(target Target, sig Signal, value int) error
symbols.doc:
SendValue queues sig with value to the process target (rt_sigqueueinfo(2) on
Linux, sigqueue(2) on FreeBSD): a realtime signal queues instead of
coalescing, and a C receiver reads the value from si_value — a Go one cannot.
It returns SIGNAL_FAILED wrapping the errno (ESRCH for a reaped pid), and
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM elsewhere.

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.doc:
Signal is a typed, platform-portable OS signal. It aliases the domain type, so
a value parsed here interoperates with the rest of the SDK process domain.

symbols.name: Target
symbols.doc:
Target names the recipient of a relayed signal: a positive value is a pid; a
value below -1 addresses the process group whose id is its absolute value.

symbols.name: CheckName
symbols.doc:
CheckName refuses with InvalidFDName a descriptor name LISTEN_FDNAMES cannot
carry: longer than systemd's FDNAME_MAX, a byte that is not printable ASCII, or
a ':'.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidFDName
symbols.doc: CodeInvalidFDName is the code of InvalidFDName.

symbols.name: Files
symbols.doc:
Files returns the inherited listening sockets (fd 3..3+LISTEN_FDS) as *os.File,
honouring LISTEN_PID. When unsetEnv is true the activation environment is
cleared so a grandchild does not re-inherit it. An empty or foreign activation
set yields nil with no error; off Unix it returns UnsupportedPlatform. Each
socket is close-on-exec, as sd_listen_fds(3) leaves it: a spawned child
inherits one only when it is passed explicitly, through Prepare or ExtraFiles.

symbols.name: InvalidFDName

code.public: The descriptor name is not valid

symbols.doc: InvalidFDName is returned for a descriptor name LISTEN_FDNAMES cannot carry.

symbols.name: Listeners
symbols.doc:
Listeners returns the inherited stream sockets wrapped as net.Listener (the
underlying *os.File is closed after the dup). Same gating and platform
behaviour as Files.

symbols.name: NamedFile
symbols.doc:
NamedFile is one descriptor PrepareFiles hands a child and its
LISTEN_FDNAMES name. It aliases the service's type.

symbols.name: Prepare
symbols.doc:
Prepare (activator side) appends each named listener's socket to child as an
inherited fd and sets LISTEN_FDS / LISTEN_FDNAMES in child.Env so the spawned
process recovers them via Files/Listeners. Off Unix it returns
UnsupportedPlatform.

symbols.name: PrepareFiles
symbols.doc:
PrepareFiles (activator side) hands files to child at fd 3 on, in order, with
LISTEN_FDS, LISTEN_FDNAMES and LISTEN_PID set as Prepare sets them — never
duplicating nor closing them, so a descriptor store hands the same ones to
each restart. Off Unix it returns UnsupportedPlatform.

symbols.name: Spec
symbols.doc:
Spec is the process spawn specification an activator augments via Prepare. It
aliases the core port type, so the same value drives process.Start.

symbols.name: WithNames
symbols.doc:
WithNames returns the inherited sockets grouped by their LISTEN_FDNAMES name;
duplicate names group several fds under one key.

symbols.name: Descriptors
symbols.doc:
Descriptors are the descriptors one datagram brought — FDSTORE=1's, the
BARRIER=1 one, the MAINPIDFD=1 pidfd, a pidfd on the sender —, the caller's
to keep or close. It is an alias of the core port's DescriptorsValue.

symbols.name: Listen
symbols.spelled: func() (l Listener, socketPath string, err error)
symbols.doc:
Listen creates a supervisor-side sd_notify socket and returns the Listener plus
the socketPath a child should be given via NOTIFY_SOCKET. Off Linux and
FreeBSD it returns the UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM error.

symbols.name: ListenFor
symbols.spelled: func(uid int, gid int) (l Listener, socketPath string, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(uid int, gid int) (l github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/systemd/notify.Listener, socketPath string, err error)
symbols.doc:
ListenFor is Listen for a service that runs as uid and gid: the socket's
private directory and the socket belong to that user, so only it and root
reach the socket. Off Linux and FreeBSD it returns the UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM
error.

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.doc:
Listener is the supervisor side of the protocol: it owns the datagram socket a
supervised child writes readiness to and yields one parsed, credential-verified
Notification per Recv.

symbols.name: MainPID
symbols.doc: MainPID advertises the main process PID to the supervisor (MAINPID=pid).

symbols.name: Notification
symbols.doc:
Notification is a parsed sd_notify datagram: the raw State field set plus the
typed Status, MainPID, and kernel-verified SenderPID, SenderUID and
SenderGID, the Descriptors it brought, with Ready/Reloading/Stopping/Watchdog
lifecycle accessors.

symbols.name: Notify
symbols.doc:
Notify sends an sd_notify datagram carrying the given NAME=value state to
$NOTIFY_SOCKET, or is a no-op returning nil when $NOTIFY_SOCKET is unset.

symbols.name: Ready
symbols.doc: Ready notifies the supervisor that startup is complete (READY=1).

symbols.name: Reloading
symbols.doc:
Reloading notifies the supervisor that a configuration reload has begun
(RELOADING=1).

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status publishes a single-line free-text status (STATUS=msg).

symbols.name: Stopping
symbols.doc: Stopping notifies the supervisor that shutdown has begun (STOPPING=1).

symbols.name: Watchdog
symbols.doc: Watchdog sends a watchdog keep-alive ping (WATCHDOG=1).

symbols.name: WatchdogInterval
symbols.doc:
WatchdogInterval reports the watchdog ping interval the supervisor configured
via $WATCHDOG_USEC; ok is false when the variable is unset, malformed or out
of a time.Duration's range, or when $WATCHDOG_PID names another process.
When ok is true, d is positive.
